sets.title: Impersonal Construction Types
sets.description: Identify impersonal construction types and sort them by category
sets.descriptionRussian: Определите типы безличных конструкций и рассортируйте их

items.prompt: Which sentence is an impersonal construction?
items.promptEnglish: Identify the subjectless sentence.
items.hint: Impersonal constructions have no grammatical subject in the nominative.
items.explanation: Мне скучно is impersonal: the experiencer (мне) is in dative, and there is no nominative subject. The others all have a nominative subject (он, скука, фильм).

items.prompt: What case is the experiencer in: "Ему было холодно"?
items.promptEnglish: What case is ему?
items.hint: The person experiencing the state in impersonal sentences takes the dative.
items.explanation: In impersonal constructions with state words (холодно, скучно, весело), the experiencer is always in the dative: ему, мне, тебе.

items.prompt: "Светает." What type of impersonal construction is this?
items.promptEnglish: Dawn is breaking.
items.hint: Verbs describing natural phenomena with no subject at all.
items.explanation: Светает (it's getting light) is a weather/nature impersonal verb. No subject exists, not even an implied one.

items.prompt: "Нам нужно уходить." What type of impersonal construction is this?
items.promptEnglish: We need to leave.
items.hint: Нужно + infinitive expresses necessity.
items.explanation: Нужно + infinitive is a modal impersonal construction expressing necessity. The experiencer нам is in the dative.

items.prompt: Which word means "it is forbidden / one must not"?
items.promptEnglish: Which modal word expresses prohibition?
items.hint: This word can mean both 'it is impossible' and 'it is forbidden.'
items.explanation: Нельзя means 'one cannot / one must not.' With imperfective infinitive it means prohibition; with perfective it means impossibility.

items.prompt: "Трудно понять этот текст." What type of impersonal construction?
items.promptEnglish: It's hard to understand this text.
items.hint: Трудно/легко/интересно + infinitive evaluate the difficulty or quality of an action.
items.explanation: Evaluative impersonals use adverbs like трудно, легко, интересно + infinitive to assess an action. No grammatical subject.

items.prompt: "Ничего не видно." What makes this construction impersonal?
items.promptEnglish: Nothing is visible.
items.hint: Look for who or what is doing the action. Is there a subject in nominative?
items.explanation: Ничего не видно has no nominative subject. Видно is an impersonal predicate, and ничего is in the genitive (negative context).

items.prompt: How do you form the past tense of "Мне холодно"?
items.promptEnglish: I am cold -> I was cold
items.hint: Impersonal past uses neuter было, not masculine or feminine.
items.explanation: Impersonal past tense always uses neuter было: Мне было холодно. There is no subject to agree with, so the default neuter form is used.

items.prompt: "Вечереет." When would you use this verb?
items.promptEnglish: It's getting dark / evening is falling.
options: When someone is tired in the evening
When describing evening approaching as a natural process
items.answer: When describing evening approaching as a natural process
items.hint: This is a weather/nature impersonal verb like светает and темнеет.
items.explanation: Вечереет describes evening falling as a natural, subjectless process. Like светает (dawn breaks) and темнеет (it gets dark), these verbs have no subject.

items.prompt: What is the difference between "нельзя курить" and "нельзя прочитать"?
items.promptEnglish: Нельзя + imperfective vs. нельзя + perfective
items.hint: The aspect of the infinitive after нельзя changes the meaning entirely.
items.explanation: Нельзя курить (impf) = smoking is forbidden/prohibited. Нельзя прочитать (pf) = it is impossible to read. Aspect shifts meaning from prohibition to impossibility.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these sentences by impersonal construction type

sets.title: Dative and Modal Practice
sets.description: Practice dative experiencers and modal impersonal words through minimal pairs and fill-in-the-blank
sets.descriptionRussian: Практикуйте дательный падеж и модальные слова

minimalPairs.explanation: Можно = 'is it permitted / may one?' Asking for permission. Нельзя would mean 'it is forbidden.'
Нельзя + imperfective infinitive = prohibition. Smoking is not allowed here.

minimalPairs.context: Ей _____ уйти пораньше. (She needs to leave early.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Надо + infinitive = necessity. Ей надо уйти = she needs to leave.

minimalPairs.context: Ей _____ уйти пораньше. (She is permitted to leave early.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Можно + infinitive = permission. Ей можно уйти = she is allowed to leave.
In impersonal constructions, the experiencer takes the dative: ему (not nominative он).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: He got cold. (personal construction with subject)
minimalPairs.explanation: Замёрз is a personal verb that takes a nominative subject: Он замёрз. Compare with impersonal Ему холодно.

minimalPairs.context: Мне _____ идти. (I have to go. - stronger obligation)
minimalPairs.explanation: Нужно expresses strong necessity or obligation: I need/have to go.

minimalPairs.context: Мне _____ идти? (May I go? - requesting permission)
minimalPairs.explanation: Можно in a question = asking permission: May I go?

blanks: _____ было страшно во время грозы. (She was scared during the storm.)
_____ нужно закончить отчёт к пятнице. (We need to finish the report by Friday.)
Здесь _____ фотографировать. (It is forbidden to take photos here.)
_____ было весело на вечеринке. (They had fun at the party.)
_____ трудно было решить эту задачу. (It was hard for me to solve this problem.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Dative experiencers and modal words in impersonal constructions
explanations: Ей (dative of она) was scared: Ей было страшно. The experiencer takes the dative.
Нам (dative of мы) need to: Нам нужно. Modal impersonal with dative experiencer.
Нельзя + imperfective infinitive = prohibition: photography is forbidden here.
Им (dative of они) had fun: Им было весело. Past tense uses neuter было.
Надо + infinitive = advice or mild obligation: you should rest.
Мне (dative of я) found it hard: Мне трудно было. Evaluative impersonal with dative.

items.prompt: Студентам _____ пользоваться словарём на экзамене. (Students are not allowed to use a dictionary.)
items.promptEnglish: Students are forbidden from using a dictionary on the exam.
items.hint: Prohibition = нельзя.
items.explanation: Нельзя + imperfective infinitive = prohibition. Students must not use a dictionary.

items.prompt: Ребёнку _____ гулять одному в парке. (The child is not allowed to walk alone.)
items.promptEnglish: The child is not permitted to walk alone in the park.
items.hint: Prohibition for a child walking alone.
items.explanation: Нельзя = prohibition. The child must not walk alone. Dative ребёнку + нельзя + imperfective infinitive.

items.prompt: _____ надо поговорить. (We need to talk.)
items.promptEnglish: We need to talk.
items.hint: The experiencer in a modal impersonal takes the dative.
items.explanation: Нам (dative of мы) with надо: Нам надо поговорить. Not nominative мы.

items.prompt: Тебе _____ заниматься каждый день. (You need to study every day.)
items.promptEnglish: You need to study every day.
items.hint: Expressing necessity or strong recommendation.
items.explanation: Нужно + infinitive = necessity. Тебе нужно заниматься = you need to study.

items.prompt: Вам _____ здесь остановиться? (Are you allowed to stop here?)
items.promptEnglish: May you stop here? (asking about permission)
items.hint: Asking about permission = можно in a question.
items.explanation: Можно in a question asks about permission: Вам можно? = Are you allowed?

sets.title: Build and Translate
sets.description: Build impersonal sentences from parts and translate them
sets.descriptionRussian: Составьте безличные предложения и переведите их

translation.english: It was fun for us at the concert.
translation.hint: Dative experiencer + было + state adverb + location

translation.english: You are not allowed to enter without a ticket.
It is easy to make a mistake here.
I need to call my parents.
Nothing could be seen in the fog.
translation.answer: В тумане ничего не было видно.
acceptableVariants: Ничего не было видно в тумане.
translation.hint: Negative impersonal in past: ничего не было видно
translation.grammarFocus: Negative impersonal predicate in past tense

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: All impersonal construction types mixed in varied exercises
sets.descriptionRussian: Все типы безличных конструкций в разных упражнениях

items.prompt: _____ интересно изучать иностранные языки. (It's interesting to study foreign languages.)
items.promptEnglish: Fill in the blank to complete this evaluative impersonal.
items.hint: The experiencer in an evaluative impersonal takes the dative.
items.explanation: Мне интересно: dative experiencer + evaluative adverb + infinitive. Not nominative я or это.

items.prompt: Ему было _____ на лекции. (He was bored at the lecture.)
items.promptEnglish: What state word completes this?
items.hint: Impersonal state words are adverbs (short form), not adjectives or nouns.
items.explanation: Скучно (adverb/predicate) in impersonal: Ему было скучно. Not скучный (adjective) or скука (noun).

items.prompt: Утром рано _____. (It gets light early in the morning.)
items.promptEnglish: Which weather verb fits?
items.hint: Which verb describes dawn, the morning light appearing?
items.explanation: Светает = it's getting light (dawn). Темнеет = getting dark, вечереет = evening falling, холодает = getting colder.

items.prompt: Нельзя _____ этот текст без словаря. (It's impossible to understand.)
items.promptEnglish: Нельзя + perfective = impossibility. Which infinitive?
items.hint: Нельзя + perfective infinitive = impossibility.
items.explanation: Нельзя + perfective понять = impossibility (cannot understand). With imperfective понимать it would mean prohibition.

items.prompt: _____ рано темнеет, а летом поздно. (In winter it gets dark early.)
items.promptEnglish: Which time expression completes the weather impersonal?
items.hint: The contrast is with летом (in summer), so what season is the opposite?
items.explanation: Зимой рано темнеет, а летом поздно. Winter vs. summer contrast with the impersonal weather verb темнеет.

items.prompt: Мне _____ было вставать в 5 утра. (I had to get up at 5 AM.)
items.promptEnglish: Which modal word expresses past necessity?
items.hint: Past necessity that actually happened (had to) = пришлось.
items.explanation: Пришлось (past of приходиться) = had to, was forced to. Мне пришлось = I had to. Stronger than надо было.

items.prompt: Легко _____, но трудно _____. (Easy to promise, hard to do.)
items.promptEnglish: Complete this Russian proverb-like evaluative impersonal.
items.hint: Evaluative impersonals use infinitives: легко + infinitive, трудно + infinitive.
items.explanation: Легко обещать, но трудно сделать. Evaluative impersonals take infinitives. This captures a universal truth.

items.prompt: В комнате _____ тихо. Ничего не слышно. (It was quiet. Nothing could be heard.)
items.promptEnglish: Past tense of an impersonal state.
items.hint: Impersonal past always uses neuter было.
items.explanation: Impersonal past = neuter было, regardless of surrounding nouns: В комнате было тихо.

items.prompt: Детям _____ играть на дороге. (Children are not allowed to play on the road.)
items.promptEnglish: Prohibition for children.
items.hint: Prohibition = нельзя + imperfective infinitive.
items.explanation: Нельзя играть = it is forbidden to play. Imperfective infinitive with нельзя expresses prohibition.

errorCorrection.hint: The experiencer in an impersonal construction takes the dative, not nominative.
errorCorrection.explanation: Impersonal states require dative: Мне холодно (not Я холодно). There is no nominative subject.

errorCorrection.hint: Impersonal past tense always uses neuter form, regardless of the experiencer's gender.
errorCorrection.explanation: Always neuter было in impersonal past: Мне было скучно. Not была (feminine) even if the speaker is female.

errorCorrection.sentence: Нельзя понимать этот текст без контекста. (meant: it's impossible to understand)
errorCorrection.hint: Нельзя + imperfective = prohibition. For impossibility, use perfective.
errorCorrection.explanation: Нельзя понимать = it's forbidden to understand (absurd). Нельзя понять = it's impossible to understand (correct meaning).

errorCorrection.hint: After modal words (нужно, надо, можно), the verb must be in the infinitive.
errorCorrection.explanation: Modal impersonals require infinitive: нужно работать (not работает). The modal word replaces the conjugation.

patternRecognition.sentence: Мне холодно. / Ей грустно. / Нам весело. / Тебе жарко.
patternRecognition.question: What structural pattern do all four sentences share?
patternRecognition.explanation: All four use dative pronoun (мне, ей, нам, тебе) + a state adverb (холодно, грустно, весело, жарко). No nominative subject.

patternRecognition.question: What do these verbs have in common?
options: They are impersonal weather/nature verbs with no subject
patternRecognition.answer: They are impersonal weather/nature verbs with no subject
patternRecognition.explanation: These are impersonal verbs describing natural phenomena. They have no grammatical subject at all, not even an implied one.

patternRecognition.sentence: Надо учиться. / Нужно работать. / Можно отдохнуть. / Нельзя опаздывать.
patternRecognition.question: What structural element follows every modal word here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Modal impersonal words (надо, нужно, можно, нельзя) are always followed by an infinitive: учиться, работать, отдохнуть, опаздывать.

minimalPairs.context: Здесь нельзя _____. (It is forbidden to swim here.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Нельзя + imperfective купаться = prohibition (swimming is forbidden). Perfective искупаться would mean impossibility.

minimalPairs.context: Здесь нельзя _____. (It is impossible to swim here - the water is too cold.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Impossibility: the water makes swimming impossible.
minimalPairs.explanation: Нельзя + perfective искупаться = impossibility (impossible to swim, e.g., water too cold). Imperfective would mean prohibition.

minimalPairs.context: _____ надо было позвонить. (I should have called.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Past necessity: I needed to call.
minimalPairs.explanation: Impersonal modal in past: Мне надо было позвонить. Dative мне, not nominative я.
Personal construction with a regular verb: Я позвонил. Nominative subject, not dative.
